advisory.finding: The dispatch's `except probe_mod.ProbeConfigError` catches the class from the `_load('inbound_probe', ...)` module instance (sys.modules key 'inbound_probe'), but the real `JiraBackend.probe_remote` -> `jira_probe.probe` -> `_resolve_env` raises `ProbeConfigError` imported via `from rebar_reconciler.inbound_probe import ...` (sys.modules key 'rebar_reconciler.inbound_probe'), a DISTINCT class object. Because `except` matches by class identity/subclass (not by value like StrEnum), the missing-env `ProbeConfigError` will NOT be caught and will propagate, aborting the whole differ pass — regressing the documented 'treat as unreachable; do not abort the pass' behavior.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make inbound-probe branch/vocabulary comparisons rely on a single canonical `inbound_probe` module instance rather than value-equality across two sys.modules keys.
evidence: inbound_probe.py:32 `class ProbeBranch(StrEnum):` — value-based equality is the only thing bridging the two module instances
adapters/jira/probe.py builds results with `rebar_reconciler.inbound_probe.ProbeBranch` (package import) while dispatch/route use the by-path instance
advisory.finding: The (inbound, probe) branch classification in `route_inbound_probe` compares `probe_result.branch` (a `ProbeBranch` from the package-import module via `jira_probe`) against `probe_mod.ProbeBranch.*` (from the `_load`-instance module). This only works because `StrEnum` compares by string value; if `ProbeBranch` were ever changed away from `StrEnum`, or a non-StrEnum branch field were introduced, the cross-module identity split would silently route every branch to the defensive 'unknown branch' fallback (no follow-on). This latent fragility mirrors the ProbeConfigError bug and should be made robust rather than depending on StrEnum value-equality.
